system.description: Named for a Slavic word meaning "black god," this power lets a Lasombra literally blot out the sun. Moon, stars and sun alike vanish beneath an inky shroud stretching horizon to horizon; even open flame seems dim and weak beneath it. While the darkness holds, the wielder may walk abroad at midday and suffer no ill effects from the sun. The blackness otherwise behaves as that summoned by Nocturne. Only three Lasombra have ever demonstrated mastery of this power — Lasombra himself, Montano, and a Magister of Greek heritage once known as Boukephos — and none of the three will teach it.
system.source: Libellus Sanguinis I: Masters of the State, Book One: Magisters
